extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff, and patent prosecution/legal staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing merger, stay, conduct, conclusion, and publication of merged reissue applications and ex parte reexamination proceedings, including interactions with concurrent litigation and required examiner/OPLA actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to merge or stay reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to merge a reissue application examination and an ex parte reexamination proceeding, consideration will be given to the status of the reissue application (e.g., whether examination has begun or it is on appeal to the Board or courts) and the status of the reexamination (e.g., on appeal or Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue examination has not begun or no appeal is pending, merger is likely. If reissue application is on appeal to the Board or courts, that fact will be considered in making the decision whether to merge or stay one of the proceedings. See In re Stoddard and In re Scragg for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain identical claims in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments/claims in the reissue application and the reexamination file for purposes of the merged proceedings (see 37 CFR 1.565(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present when merger is ordered, the patent owner will be required to submit a 'housekeeping' amendment placing the same amendments in both proceedings; such amendment must not address patentability. Amendments in merged proceedings are submitted under 37 CFR 1.173 in accordance with reissue practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping amendment must not address patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Housekeeping amendments filed solely to make claims identical in merged files must not address any issue of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such housekeeping amendments may be accomplished by amending either or both proceedings, but must be limited to harmonizing text. If not timely submitted, any claim not identical across merged files should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 2, as indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of reexamination while reissue examination proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: If reissue application examination has progressed to a point where merger is not desirable at that time, the reexamination proceeding will generally be stayed until the reissue application examination is complete on the issues then pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completion of reissue examination on the pending issues, the stay will be removed and proceedings will be merged if reissue is pending; if reissue became abandoned, reexamination will continue separately. Reissue examination may be reopened if necessary for merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory response periods after stay removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stay of a reexamination proceeding has been removed following reissue application examination, the first Office action will set a shortened statutory period of 1 month for response (unless longer clearly warranted); the second Office action will normally be final and also set a 1-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These shortened periods are used to prevent undue delay and to proceed with 'special dispatch' following the earlier stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue patent issuance serves as reexamination certificate when merged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding are merged, the issuance of the reissue patent will also serve as the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 and the reissue patent will so indicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification to OPLA when reissue filed during/after reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is filed after an ex parte reexamination request, the OPLA should be notified as promptly as possible after the reissue application reaches the Technology Center (TC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination will be made whether reexamination should be ordered; if reexamination is ordered, no first Office action will accompany the decision ordering reexamination. If any of the files are paper files, they should be hand-delivered to OPLA with the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of issues proper for reexamination when deciding merger
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to merge, consideration will be given as to whether issues raised in the reissue application would not be proper for consideration in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider the status of reexamination (e.g., appeal to Board or court, Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate) in making merger/stay decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate examiner assignment for merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to examiner assignment of the merged reexamination/reissue proceeding, applicable assignment rules (see MPEP § 2236) must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single joint Office action and entry in both files
rubrics_metrics.description: In any merged reissue application and reexamination proceeding, each Office action issued by the examiner will take the form of a single action which jointly applies to both the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, and each action will be physically entered into both files (which remain separate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses by the applicant/patent owner in such a merged proceeding must be a single response filed in duplicate for entry in both files (or multiple copies if multiple reexaminations are merged) and service must be made on any third-party requester. A copy of all Office actions will be mailed to the third-party requester but not to any other third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of merged proceeding for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action in a merged proceeding, the merged proceeding will be terminated and the reissue application held abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A NIRC (Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate) will be issued (see MPEP § 2287), and the Director will proceed to issue a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 in accordance with the last Office action unless further action is clearly needed in view of rule differences between reexamination and reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of express abandonment or CPA on merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner files an express abandonment of the reissue application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.138, the next Office action will accept the abandonment, dissolve the merged proceeding, and continue the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a continued prosecution reissue application (CPA) is filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) causing express abandonment of the existing reissue, this will likely dissolve the merged proceeding, stay the CPA, and continue separate reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/adjustment of grounds after dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the merged proceeding is dissolved based on abandonment of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding continues, any grounds of rejection not applicable under reexamination should be withdrawn; new grounds applicable under reexamination should be made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions remaining which cannot be considered under reexamination following dissolution should be noted as not proper under reexamination (37 CFR 1.552(c)). Continuation reissue applications might not be merged to prevent delay tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE does not expressly abandon reissue application in merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant files a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) of the reissue application under 37 CFR 1.114, the reissue application is not considered expressly abandoned; finality of the Office action is withdrawn and the merged proceeding will continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is because an RCE is not an abandonment of any application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge or stay should not be filed before reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of them because of the other, should be filed before an order directing reexamination is issued; such premature petitions will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition filed prior to determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will be returned by the CRU or TC Director and noted in both files; see MPEP § 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition to merge or stay after reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or stay at the time of the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or thereafter if the Office has not acted. A reexamination requester who is not the patent owner may petition as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535. Petitions by parties other than the patent owner or requester will be returned as improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All petitions to merge or stay filed by the patent owner or third-party requester subsequent to the date of the order for reexamination will be referred to the OPLA for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single fee treatment in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper requiring payment of a fee is filed (e.g., excess claim fee, extension fee, petition fee, appeal/brief/oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid even though copies must be filed for each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As to excess claim fees, reissue practice will control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited handling for court-ordered/sanctioned reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request indicates it is filed as a result of a court order or a court-sanctioned agreement, or litigation is stayed for filing a reexamination request, the request will be taken up 6 weeks after filing and all aspects of the proceeding will be expedited to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, subsequent examination after patent owner statement (1.530) and requester reply (1.535) will be expedited; Office actions will normally set a 1-month shortened statutory period for response rather than the usual 2 months. Response periods may be extended only upon a 'strong' showing of sufficient cause (see MPEP § 2265).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Federal court decisions known at determination time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal Court decision on the merits of a patent is known to the examiner when determining whether a substantial new question (SNQ) exists, the existence of a final court decision of claim validity does not necessarily mean no SNQ is present because the Office uses different standards of proof and claim interpretation than courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final holdings are not controlling; a final holding of invalidity/unenforceability (after all appeals) is controlling and would mean no SNQ as to claims held invalid/unenforceable. Any determination after a Federal Court decision must be reviewed by the CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE) to ensure conformity with Office litigation policy (see MPEP § 2240).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of Office determination from district court outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will make its determination of SNQ independently of a district court's decision because district courts and the Office apply different evidentiary standards (e.g., 'clear and convincing' vs. 'preponderance of the evidence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue preclusion cannot generally be applied against the Office based on a district court holding since the Office was not a party to the earlier proceeding (see Trans Texas Holdings and Translogic examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify Office of court decisions during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.565(a), the patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must promptly notify the Office of any Federal court decision involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Office becomes aware of a court decision, the order to reexamine is reviewed to determine if a SNQ still exists; if not, the order may be vacated by the CRU or TC Director and reexamination concluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of final court decisions on reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A final Federal Court holding of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is binding on the Office: claims held invalid/unenforceable will be withdrawn from reexamination; reexamination continues as to remaining claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims being examined are finally held invalid/unenforceable, the reexamination will be vacated by the CRU or TC Director as no longer containing a SNQ. Conversely, a final court holding upholding validity does not bind the Office (Ethicon v. Quigg) although deference may be accorded to court factual findings where evidence is the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 22.20 when claims held invalid by court
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are held invalid by a court and are no longer being reexamined, form paragraph 22.20 ('Claims Held Invalid By Court, No Longer Being Reexamined') should be used at the beginning of the Office action, with specified bracketed insertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner note provides instructions for inserting claim numbers, patentee, decision citation, and court name in the appropriate brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation review duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation for evidence of prior or concurrent litigation involving the patent for which ex parte reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation includes review of reexamination and patent files and results of the litigation computer search by the STIC. If litigation or a Federal court decision is discovered, the examiner must bring the fact to the attention of the CRU SPE or TC QAS prior to further action; the CRU SPE/TC QAS must review any action to ensure current Office litigation policy is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court decision controlling as to claims finally held invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a federal court has ruled and reexamination is still appropriate under guidelines, the federal court decision will be considered controlling and followed as to claims finally held invalid by the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the ex parte reexamination proceeding, the examiner must prepare a NIRC by completing form PTOL-469 and, if appropriate, prepare an examiner’s amendment. Where claims are found patentable, reasons must be given for each claim found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must prepare the reexamination file for Data Management to prepare and issue a certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570; notify CRU SPE/TC QAS of the conclusion for panel review per MPEP § 2271.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU SPE/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference to review patentability of the claim(s) before a NIRC is issued; if the conference confirms the examiner’s decision, the NIRC is issued and signed by the examiner with two conferees initialing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conferees initial even if one dissents. If the conference does not confirm patentability, the examiner must reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action rejecting the claims not confirmed. Panel review is not held for claims that were in the case when the Board or court decided the appeal on the merits, nor when proceeding is to be concluded by cancellation of all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC consequences and post-termination filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A NIRC informs the patent owner and any third-party requester that the reexamination prosecution has been terminated; the rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed after prosecution has been terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, IDS, or other paper related to the merits filed after prosecution termination must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to have it considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract changes in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the title will not need to be changed during reexamination; if change is necessary, notify patent owner to provide an amendment changing the title early. If all claims are found patentable and a NIRC is or will be mailed, the examiner may change the title only by examiner’s amendment; merely initialing a change is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s amendment can be made to change the abstract when narrowing amendments have changed the focus of the invention (e.g., claim made more specific and abstract no longer reflects specific limitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of claim(s) and drawing figure for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative claim and an appropriate drawing figure are to be indicated for publication in the Official Gazette; the broadest claim should be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should ordinarily designate one claim on each invention; in regular prosecution up to five may be designated for publication when multiple inventions exist, but in reexamination the examiner must select only one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing IFW and file jacket data before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publication of the reexamination certificate, the examiner must review reexamination and patent files to ensure appropriate parts are completed: SEARCHED and SEARCH NOTES in IFW Search Notes form; IFW file jacket Litigation Review and Copending Office Proceedings boxes; Bibliographic Data Sheet; Issue Classification IFW form with status and final claim numbers and current international and U.S. classification for original classification and cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of the Issue Classification box is required even if all claims are canceled.
